rgb: The five frames show a steeply downward-angled egocentric view of a gravelly, stone-covered outdoor ground surface, with a small sliver of sky and sloped terrain visible only at the upper-left edge of the first frame. Another person wearing brown strappy sandals stands roughly 3 to 5 metres in front of the camera wearer, with only their bare lower legs and feet visible near the top of the frame while their torso and head remain completely out of view above the top edge, preventing direct observation of their gaze. Their feet are angled generally away from the camera wearer and slightly toward the camera's right, while the camera wearer's own forearms, hands, and blue-shoed left foot occupy the bottom foreground roughly 3 to 5 metres below the camera. Between the first and third frames, the camera pitches further downward and moves away from the ground, shifting the other person's feet into the upper-right quadrant and placing the stones and shell fragments on the ground directly in front of the camera wearer's left foot out of arm's reach. In the third and fourth frames, the camera wearer extends their left hand backward and up away from the ground about 3 to 5 metres behind their left foot while their right hand stays low on the right near a flat white shell fragment, and in the fifth frame the left hand lowers into the left foreground about 3 to 5 metres from the lens holding a small white object that partially occludes the gravel behind it.
depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-facing outdoor scene over a sloped rocky ground plane (~3–5 m below the camera), showing the camera wearer's own forearms, hands, and blue-shoed left leg at the bottom (brightest, ~3–5 m away) and another person's lower legs and sandal-clad feet in front and to the upper-right (~3–5 m away, ~3–5 m from the wearer's feet). Both people have their upper bodies and heads cropped out of view, with the other person's feet angled backward and slightly left relative to the camera wearer, while the ground pebbles and a small round white stone held out of arm's reach (~3–5 m) are directly below. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer crouches or leans down as their left hand moves away from the ground (~3–5 m in frames 3–4) and lowers the stone far from the lens (~3–5 m on the left in frame 5), while the other person's legs shift toward the top-right edge and fade into darker depth values. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the wearer's lowered left arm and leg from the camouflaged rocky terrain, though it is unreliable along the outer fisheye corners (which turn black) and in frame 5 where the other person's feet nearly vanish into the background gradient.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground human limbs against the unlabelled rocky ground, placing the other person's lower legs and feet in the upper-right (~3–5 m away, angled away from the camera wearer's left) and the camera wearer's own hands, forearms, and left leg at the bottom (~3–5 m away, out of arm's reach). Both individuals' torsos and heads are out of view, so gaze cannot be observed from the masks, though foot orientation shows the wearer facing backward/upward away from the other person's legs (~3–5 m ahead). Over the 5 frames, the other person's leg mask approaches from the upper-right frame boundary as the wearer's left arm extends backward away from the ground in frames 3–4 and lowers on the left in frame 5, where the small white stone pinched between the fingers is segmented and labelled as a 'sports ball' (~3–5 m away). This map highlights the exact silhouette of the held object and limb boundaries against the cluttered pebbles better than RGB alone, but it is unreliable in splitting the camera wearer's own body parts into multiple separate 'person' instances with inconsistent colours and straight horizontal cutoffs across the left forearm in frames 4–5.
pose: The pose map renders only magenta 2D hand skeletons on a black background, capturing the camera wearer's hands in the lower foreground (~3–5 m away, out of immediate arm's reach) while omitting all body skeletons, legs, feet, and the rocky ground layout. In frame 1, only the wearer's hands overlap at the bottom-right (~3–5 m away); in frames 2 and 4, both the right hand (bottom-right, ~3–5 m) and left hand (bottom-centre/left, ~3–5 m, ~3–5 m apart) are tracked, whereas in frame 3 only the right hand and in frame 5 only the lowered left hand (middle-left, ~3–5 m away) appear. Because no upper bodies, heads, or the other person's legs (~3–5 m ahead in the upper-right) are detected due to heavy out-of-frame cropping, facing direction and gaze cannot be determined from this map alone. Across the sequence, the tracked skeletons show the left hand moving backward away from the ground and then lowering downward and opening its fingers away from the camera in frame 5; this makes fine finger articulation and pinch posture much clearer than in the RGB strip, but the map is unreliable when the retreating left hand is completely missed in frame 3 and the right hand is missed in frame 5.
